title: Tikkun is in the vessels: a thing and its opposite as one
overview:
Chapter 31 turns to the advantage of the vessels over the lights: there is more *hiskalelus* (inclusion) in the vessels, and that is the main thing of *Tikkun*. A light of *chesed* cannot bear *din*, yet it can shine in a vessel of *gevura*, so the inclusion must come from the vessel. The body shows it (one organ is cured through another, eyes water from onions), and so do thought, speech and action: the further out, the easier it is to smile at someone you would like to kill. In actual deed nothing is pure: water has some fire in it, and even a death sentence, Haman's, takes time to pass through the vessels, and the delay is a *chesed*.

Then a contradiction: the vessel yields to its opposite light because of the inner intention, the Name *MaH* rooted in the *Kav*, as Yael's smile and the salesman's must come from inside. So inclusion is in the inner side of the vessels, while their outside, from the limiting power of the *makif*, does one mission and works miracles in the physical place. That same power divides, and division of labor, as in an army, is what makes *Tikkun*.

sections.title: Tikkun comes from the vessels, because only vessels hold opposites
sections.summary: The vessels have an advantage over the lights: there is more *hiskalelus* (inclusion) in them, and that is the main thing of *Tikkun*. The proof is that the light of *chesed* can shine in a vessel of *gevura*: a light cannot join its opposite, so it must be the vessel.

phrases.he: (לא) והנה יש יתרון מעלה בבחינת הכלים מבחינת האורות, ממה שיש בחינת ההתכללות בכלים יותר מבאורות,
שזהו עיקר בחינת התיקון
phrases.en: That's the main thing of *Tikkun*: it comes *davka* from the *kelim*.

phrases.he: כידוע דעיקר בחינת התיקון הוא בא מריבוי הכלים כו'
phrases.en: The whole thing of *Tikkun* is *ribui hakelim*.

phrases.he: ודוקא על ידי בחינת חיצוניות הכלי, שהוא בחינת נה''י כו'

blocks.text: The *kelim* (vessels) have more *hiskalelus* (inclusion) than the *oros* (lights), the main thing of *Tikkun* (the world of Repair): it comes *davka* (precisely) from many vessels and their outside, *Nehi*, as with the explanations in front of them, so many, *davka* in the external letters.

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שמצינו בכמה מקומות דאור החסד יוכל להאיר בכלי הגבורה ואור הגבורה בכלי החסד ואם כן, מה שיחליף האור להאיר בכלי היפוכו,
אם היה זה מצד עצמו למה לא יוכלל ויחובר באור היפוכו המנגדו?
phrases.en: If it was from the side of the light, why can't the light get conjoined with another light?

phrases.he: כמו אור מדת החסד שלא יסבול אור מדת הדין כלל וכלל
אלא מוכרח לומר שזהו מצד בחינת הכלי, שיכול לסבול אור היפוכה המנגדה
phrases.en: It's *davka* the *kli* that can take opposite light.

phrases.he: כי יש בכלים דוקא בחינת וענין ההתכללות מדבר והיפוכו, מה שאין כן באורות כו'

blocks.text: A listener remarks that the "New and Improved Kabbalah Series" is then lights of *Tohu* (chaos) in vessels of *Tikkun*, as the Rebbe meant. It is this *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity), he agrees, the key of *Chassidus*: many vessels, *davka* their outside, explanations reaching the total external world.

The proof: the light of *chesed* (kindness) shines in the vessel of *gevura* (might), and that of *gevura* in the vessel of *chesed*, though the lights themselves cannot be joined: *chesed* cannot bear *din* (judgement) at all. So **it's *davka* the *kli* that can take opposite light**.

sections.title: The body: one organ can heal another, through the vessels
sections.summary: *Tikkun* in a person is mainly from the side of his body. One organ can be cured by treating another, because the vessels are included in one another; but a weakness in the light itself, like failing sight from old age, is not cured by strengthening the light of the heart.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר התיקון בבחינת האדם מצד גופו
phrases.en: The main *Tikkun* in a way of an *adam* is not so much from the side of the soul, but *davka* from the side of the body.

phrases.he: כמו שאנו רואים בחוש טבעי אברי האדם, שכל אחד יש בו התכללות מזולתו,
עד שיכולים להשלים חסרון א' על ידי רפואת אבר זולתו
phrases.en: You can fix one up from fixing up another one.

phrases.he: כמו לקלקול הראות בעין ירפאו לכח הגידין שברגל, שיש בהן בהתכללות מגידין שבעין

blocks.text: So a person's main *Tikkun* is *davka* from the body: each organ includes the others, so one can be healed through another, the eye through the nerves of the foot. That is acupuncture: they knew about it back then.

phrases.he: אבל לא ירפאו לאור וחיות שנחלש במוח עד שנחלש בראות מצד הזקנה וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: When the *chalishus* is from the inside, not from the *kelim*, then you can't do that.

phrases.he: על ידי חיזוק כח ואור חיות המדות שבלב,
phrases.en: Where the light of the mind is starting to go, you can't just work up some heavy *middos* and it'll help it; it won't.

phrases.he: אף על פי שהמוח ולב כלולים זה עם זה
רק מצד חיזוק כלי הלב יחזקו לכלי המוח
phrases.en: But the strengthening of the heart will actually help the brain also.

phrases.he: ויאיר כח השכל בראות יותר כו' מפני שאין לאור השכל עם אור המדות חיבור והתכללות כל כך, כמו שיש חיבור והתכללות של כלי הלב עם כלי המוח וכן כלי העין עם כלי החוטם וכלי האוזן וכהאי גוונא ולזה הטעם הנה דוקא מצד בחינת הכלי יוכל להאיר בה אור המנגדה כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: Not so when the weakness is inside, in the light of the brain, as sight fades with age: working up heavy *middos* (emotional attributes) won't help a fading mind, though brain and heart include each other. But strengthening the vessel of the heart does help the brain.

blocks.title: Exercise, and a shot for the brain
blocks.text: Exercise helps everything, the brain included. And if somebody has an infection in his brain, you can give him a shot in his *tachas* (behind); you don't have to put it straight into his brain.

sensitivity.reason: A coarse word for where the shot is given, in a medical example a reader could take as advice.
sensitivity.publishable: Exercise helps everything, the brain included. And if somebody has an infection in his brain, the treatment can be given elsewhere in the body; it doesn't have to go straight into his brain.

blocks.text: The lights of mind and *middos* are not joined as the vessels are, heart with brain, eye with nose (onions make your eyes water). So the opposing light shines through the vessel.

sections.title: Chesed and gevura in thought, speech and action: a person can act against his heart
sections.summary: *Chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite of the *middos*. Yet once they come into the vessels of thought, speech and action, a person can smile at the one he hates, and the further out the vessel, the easier: all because vessels hold a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: ויובן זה יותר במה שאנו רואים במדות חסד וגבורה
שהן הפכיים מנגדיים ממש כו'
phrases.en: From all the different *middos*, *chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite ones.

blocks.text: *Chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite *middos*. *Chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding), or *netzach* and *hod*, have opposite *tnuos* (movements) but do the same thing; *chesed* and *gevura* *mamash* (actually) do opposite things.

phrases.he: אך כאשר באין המדות בכלי, כמו למחשבה ולדבור ומעשה בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: When it comes in *kelim*, in other words, of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh* in actuality,

phrases.he: יוכל אור החסד להאיר במחשבה ודבור ומעשה היפוכו ממש שהרי יכול לחשוב ולדבר ולעשות נגד מה שבלבו

blocks.text: But in the vessels of thought, speech and action, a person can think, speak and do the very opposite of what is in his heart.

blocks.title: Yael's smile and the car salesman
blocks.text: Like Yehudis and Yael, who gave him a big smile, or the car salesman, smiling like he loves you. The further out, the easier: thinking the opposite is not so easy, saying it is easier, acting opposite to your heart is very easy.

phrases.he: וגם לכעוס בלב על אוהבו בלבו, ולרחם בלבו על שונאו כו' שהלב מוכן להיות כלי למה שהוא היפוכו כו', לפי שבכלים יש התכללות דבר והיפוכו יותר מבאורות
(דמה שבגילה יש רעדה וברוגז יש רחמים, וכן להיפך, ברעדה גילה וברחמים רוגז,
phrases.en: In happiness, there is also fear, and in anger, there's also mercy, and vice versa.

phrases.he: הכל מצד הכלי דוקא כו')
phrases.en: This is all *davka* from the *kelim*.

blocks.text: Anger at the one he loves or mercy on his enemy is possible even in the heart, being a vessel, but not easy; *adraba* (just the opposite), the more external, the easier. So happiness holds fear and anger mercy: **This is all *davka* from the *kelim***; the light of happiness itself has no fear.

sections.title: In the deed there is no pure din: the six days, the verdict, and the death sentence
sections.summary: Each of the six days has its own work, yet every day includes the others, because a day is a vessel. Whatever comes into actual deed is composite: even a sentence of death is held up by the vessels it must pass through, and the delay is already *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכך אנו מוצאים בששת ימי המעשה,
phrases.en: This we find in the six days,

phrases.he: שביום א' הוא בחינת חסד - יהי אור, וביום הב' בחינת גבורה - יהי רקיע כו',
וכמו שכתוב בזהר דכל יומא בעבידתיה כו'
phrases.en: Every day has its own special work.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בכל יום יש התכללות מיום זולתו דוקא כידוע
phrases.en: But nonetheless, you see that in every day, there's really the *inyan* of all days.

phrases.he: לפי שכאשר בא האור בכלי שנקרא יום, אז יש התכללות דבר והיפוכו דוקא

blocks.text: So with the six days of creation, which are vessels: the first *chesed*, "Let there be light", the second *gevura*, a firmament to separate. Each day has its own work, as the *Zohar* says, yet each includes all: in the vessel of a day, the light holds a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: להיות שכאשר בא הדבר לידי השפעה בפועל ממש, אי אפשר שלא יוכלל בחסד מבחינת דין ובדין מבחינת החסד
phrases.en: When a thing is in actuality, then it can't be a perfect; it has to be a *murkav*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשהאור והשפע עדיין בלא כלי כו'

blocks.text: In actual influence, *chesed* must include some *din* and *din* some *chesed*: **it has to be a *murkav*** (composite).

blocks.title: Water always has some fire in it
blocks.text: You can't have water that is just water: it has a temperature, some fire, so even room-temperature water warms a colder place; and it is even more *murkav* than that. In the total external, nothing is perfect and non-*murkav*.

phrases.he: כמו פסק דין למעשה דוקא שבהכרח יוכלל חסד בדין ודין בחסד
phrases.en: Like a *psak din* for actual *maaseh*: you can't have a totally perfect *din* or *chesed* of a *psak din*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו למעשה כו'
phrases.en: When it's not *lemaaseh*, you can say whatever you want to say.

phrases.he: ונמצא שמצד בחינת חיצוניות הכלי, שהוא למעשה, שם הוא עיקר בחינת ההתכללות כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: So a *psak din* (verdict) for a deed can't be perfect *din* or *chesed*; not *lemaaseh* (for the deed), you can say what you want. The inclusion is mainly in the outside of the vessel, the deed: most simply, in deed you can smile opposite to what you feel.

blocks.question: A death sentence: isn't that total gevura?
blocks.text: Not even that. In the Torah the death penalty is a *kapara* (atonement) for the person, really a *chesed*; and the trial itself is already a *chesed*.

blocks.title: We all saw him shoot
blocks.text: We all saw him shoot the guy; why a trial, let's lynch him? No: you can't kill him on the spot, you need a *beis din* (court), and the *beis din* is a *chesed* for him, a chance to prove something.

blocks.title: Haman, hanged without a trial
blocks.text: Even Haman, the worst case, had no trial: the king said, hang him right now, and still it took a while (they took him right out, a listener objects; no matter). From the *midas hadin* (attribute of judgement) upstairs he would have died on the spot; even a gun takes a second, and that already commutes the *din*.

blocks.question: The only Tikkun for Amalek is to break it. That's perfect din: where's the chesed?
blocks.text: A listener says it is a *chesed*: Amalek's *Tikkun* is to be broken like an earthenware vessel, pure once broken. No: that is the next thing, the lights' inclusion, where *din* at its source is *chesed*, to protect the public; even killing Amalek, the inner intention is *chesed*. But that is intention, not deed.
From the vessels it is different: the *ribui hakelim* means it takes time, so there is automatically inclusion; he does not just die as soon as you say so.

From the light, *midas hadin* would allow no world: He wanted to create it with *din*, saw it would not stand, and joined *chesed* to it (a listener corrects him: it says *rachamim*, mercy, which means just that). So from the light, *din* could not exist from the start, and a man sentenced would cease at once. Not so in deed.

Take a gun and shoot him: it still takes time, three hours there, three seconds here. He is not dead because you decided so: it goes through the vessels, which hold it up, a commutation, a delay of the *din*; and a delay of *din* is *chesed*.

And the delay allows a change: people on death row nowadays can go off it. So with Amalek: the holding up with Agag *mamash* changed something; he had a continuation. Without the many vessels, the commutation, it would be instantaneous and, as a listener says, the world would be destroyed.

blocks.title: If looks could kill
blocks.text: Achashverosh's *din* on Haman was total, yet it took time. One look at his face and Haman knew it was all over; from the lights it would have been over at once, as in Harry Potter: "if looks could kill". But they had to take him out, drag him and hang him; going through the vessels, he lived longer.

blocks.title: Vashti, had she lived a little longer
blocks.text: It could even have changed: had Vashti been kept alive a little longer, Achashverosh would have stopped being mad and kept her.

In deed, however pure, there is inclusion. Achashverosh's anger was totally pure, but being actual, it does not come out pure, and so it can diminish. In the lights it can't; only through the vessels does anger diminish, given a little time. So *davka* in the outside of the vessels is the inclusion.

sections.title: The contradiction: the vessel yields to the opposite light because of the inner intention
sections.summary: Yet what lets a light shine in its opposite vessel is the vessel's *bittul* (yielding) to the light, which comes from within, from the Name *MaH*: the inner intention, rooted in the *Kav*, where *chesed* and *gevura* are one. Yael's smile, the salesman's smile: the smile has to come from the inside of the face. So inclusion is in the inner side of the vessels, not in the deed itself, and an angel can carry only one mission.

phrases.he: אך הנה לכאורה יש סתירה לכל זה שהרי באמת, מה שהאור יוכל להאיר בכלי היפוכו, הוא מצד בחינת הביטול של הכלי לגבי האור
והוא על ידי בחינת שם מ''ה מלגאו,
phrases.en: It's really from the inner intention, from the inside.

phrases.he: שרש בחינת ההתכללות באורות,
דוקא מצד הארת הקו כו'
phrases.en: And that comes from the *haaras hakav*.

blocks.text: At first glance this is contradicted: the light shines in its opposite vessel through the vessel's *bittul* (self-nullification), by the Name *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon* (the first world): from the inner intention.

blocks.title: Yael's smile
blocks.text: Yael could smile at Sisera because of the inner intention, the *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*: the inner intention of what the *midda* would be turned it over, making the vessel *batel* (nullified) to the light.

blocks.title: The salesman's smile
blocks.text: The salesman smiles because of the inner intention: he wants to make money. (A listener offers the *goyishe* "Don't get angry, get even.") His *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon* is his self-image as the greatest salesman; so too at Disneyland.

blocks.question: What does self-image have to do with Yael?
blocks.text: Her self-image, her *Adam Kadmon*, was that she meant to kill him and would do anything for it: in the original inner intention, not in the vessel.

blocks.title: Mata Hari
blocks.text: She saw herself as a Mata Hari, ready for total *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): wanting to kill him so much that she would even look not angry and treat him nicely, and really nicely, with actual *middos*, not just vessels, or he would feel it. That made the vessels *batel* to the light: it came from the inner *MaH*.

The inner *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon* said it should be so: the light itself might not intend it, but the inner-inner intention did. And *Adam Kadmon* is a *ratzon l'ratzon* (a will for a will): a will to come up with any will needed to get the thing done.

blocks.title: I never met a man I didn't like
blocks.text: A great salesman's *Adam Kadmon* wills to like anybody (Will Rogers: "I never met a man I didn't like"), not to do him good but to find a good way to talk to him.

You see this in missionaries, who are a kind of salesmen. They work themselves up to love everybody, and really love them, but it is not really a love: it is an intention of hate. It is really an intention of *gevura*, which is control. They want to control this person.

sensitivity.reason: Says missionaries' love for the people they approach is really an intention of hate and control.

blocks.text: So too *How to Win Friends and Influence People*, a great-selling book: its very title is controlling people.
It is the intent of the intent, the *ratzon l'ratzon*, and before it the Name *MaH*: what he actually intends.

The lights' inclusion comes from the *haaras hakav* (the shining of the *Kav*, the line of light): in the *Kav*, the essence of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), *chesed* and *gevura* are one. The inner intent of *gevura* is *chesed*, and of a king's *chesed*, proper courts of law.

blocks.question: Why are they called chasidei umos haolam (the kindly of the nations), when the whole matter of the seven mitzvos, a court of law included, is davka din?
blocks.text: From this *din* comes a world of *chesed*; from *chesed*, letting anyone do as he pleases, a world of *din*.

So the inclusion comes from the lights, and the *bittul* is in the *pnimiyus hakelim* (the inner side of the vessels), which feel the inner intention and yield. A salesman's smile must come from inside his face or it looks phony: he convinces himself he feels it, though the intention is control, *gevura*.

phrases.he: ולזה הטעם, דוקא בפנימיות הכלים יש התכללות
(וכמו הכונה שבמעשה המצות שמתכלל ב' הפכים כו'
phrases.en: Like the *kavana* in the *maaseh* of the *mitzvos* that brings together two *hafachim*,

phrases.he: והיינו כמו עצמות וגידים כו'
phrases.en: and that's like the bones and the nerves that come out of them,

phrases.he: מה שאין כן גוף המעשה)
phrases.en: where in the *guf hamaaseh* it's not like that.

phrases.he: ולא בחיצוניות
שהרי אין מלאך א' עושה ב' שליחות הפכים
phrases.en: A *malach* can't do two *shlichuses*.

phrases.he: מפני שכל שליחות השפע בא מחיצוניות הכלים דוקא,
שמביא השפע לחוץ
phrases.en: that brings the *hashpaa* of it to the outside.

phrases.he: כמו חיצוניות הכלי דאותיות וכהאי גוונא
ולכך פני אריה להימין כו',
phrases.en: By the angels, you see the lion is on the right, and the ox is on the left, always.

phrases.he: לא ישנו את תפקידם
phrases.en: And they can't change.

phrases.he: ולא יתחברו להחליף מעשיהם מזה לזה כו'
phrases.en: And they won't join together to change over.

phrases.he: ולכך כל יומא בעבידתיה דווקא כו'.
phrases.en: That's why each day has its own work.

blocks.text: So the inclusion is in the inner side of the vessels: **like the *kavana* in the *maaseh* of the *mitzvos* that brings together two *hafachim*** (opposites), like bones and nerves, while the body of the deed has none.
The next tape picks up: the *kavanos* of the deed can hold two intentions together; the body of the deed is one thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 047 opens by finishing class 046's reading of line 35, before it reads line 36 (w46).

blocks.text: For one angel does not do two opposite missions. Even with *chesed* as its inner light, a vessel doing *din* does only *din*; only a light holds two opposite intentions. A smile is not a frown: an angel of a smile, even with a frown inside, does one mission.
Why? Every mission of influence goes out from the outside of the vessel, and it can go out only one way, whatever you say. Only the inside of the vessel is *batel* to the opposite.

So with the angels: the lion is always on the right and the ox on the left, and they can't take turns. A *patsch* (a slap) is a *patsch*, whether of *chesed* or of *gevura*, a vessel of *gevura* only, and a smile is a smile. **That's why each day has its own work.**

sections.title: Two sources: the inner light in the vessel, and the limiting power of the makif
sections.summary: The inner side of the vessel receives the inner light, so when the lights are included in one another so is the inside of the vessel, as in the feelings of Michael and Gavriel. The outside of the vessel comes from the limiting power of the *makif*, which bears two opposites at once: hence miracles happen in the physical place itself.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא משום דפנימית הכלי הוא מקבל מבחינת אור פנימי המוגבל בכלי,
וכאשר יש התכללות באורות, ממילא יש התכללות בפנימית הכלים,
phrases.en: When there's *hiskalelus* in the *oros*, then there can be *hiskalelus* *bepnimiyus hakelim*.

phrases.he: כמו התפעלות והשגות מיכאל וגבריאל כו'
phrases.en: Like in the *hispaalus* and *hasagos* of Michael and Gavriel.

phrases.he: וחיצוניות הכלים מבחינת הכח המגביל שבבחינת מקיף
phrases.en: The *chitzoniyus hakelim* comes from the actual *koach hamegbil*, which is in a way of a *makif*.

blocks.text: Inclusion in the lights, from the *Kav*, makes inclusion in the inner side of the vessels: the *hispaalus* and *hasagos* (excitement and grasp) of Michael and Gavriel, not their actions. The outside comes from the *koach hamegbil* (the limiting power), like a *makif* (encompassing light).

phrases.he: על כן יש בו ב' הפכים כאחד, בחינת התכללות דבר והיפוכו דוקא
phrases.en: Therefore *davka* over there you can really have a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: כמו כל הנסים, שהם דוקא בבחינת חיצוניות הכלים בפועל ממש
phrases.en: The whole thing of a *nes* is *davka* in the *chitzoniyus hakelim*.

phrases.he: כמו כל מקום שנעשה בו הנס, שהמקום הזה סובל דבר והיפוכו, מלמעלה מן הטבע בטבע כו'
phrases.en: The actual place can take a thing and its opposite, higher than the *teva* inside the *teva*.

phrases.he: כהפיכת ים ליבשה כו',
phrases.en: Like to change over the ocean to dry land.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא מקום הארון אינו מן המדה וכו', וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: So the outside holds two opposites as one. However Yael did it, she killed him: outside, the deed literally did a mission opposite to itself.

blocks.question: How does "two opposites at once" follow from the limiting power of the makif?
blocks.text: Unlike the inner light, either this or that, the *makif* is no *gvul* (limit) but a *koach hamegbil*; in it one does not know Haman from Mordechai, Esav from Yaakov: there a thing and its opposite can be.

So every *nes* (miracle) is in the actual outside of the vessels: the water stood up. The place bears a thing and its opposite, above nature inside nature, the ocean made dry land, physically, not spiritually; so too the place of the Ark took up no space, in actual measurement.

blocks.question: Is that the same thing as the mother who, in a sudden panic, can lift a car?
blocks.text: Yes: from the power of the *makif*, which comes directly, not through a *tzimtzum* (contraction).

sections.title: Division of labor: the division that makes Tikkun
sections.summary: From the *makif*'s line of measure also comes the root of *hischalkus*, each vessel separate by itself. That is the main thing of *Tikkun*: the division of labor, as in an army, makes a unity greater than any single warrior, even where all share one will.

phrases.he: וגם משם הוא בא שרש בחינת ההתחלקות, כל אחד מובדל בפני עצמו
phrases.en: And also from there comes the *shoresh* of the *hischalkus*, that each one is *muvdal* by itself.

phrases.he: שהוא בא מצד בחינת קו המדה שבמקיף, שהוא שרש הכלים המגבילים כו'

blocks.text: From there too comes the root of *hischalkus* (division): each vessel *davka* its own thing. The beginning of the line, the *kav hamida* (line of measure) in the *makif*, gives both: as said, it connects everything, holding all opposites, and separates everything, this *chesed* and this *gevura*. It is the root of the limiting vessels.

phrases.he: ולזה עיקר בחינת התיקון הוא בחינת ריבוי ההתחלקות דוקא
phrases.en: That's why it's *davka* from the divisions that come the unification.

blocks.text: So *Tikkun* is many divisions: **that's why it's *davka* from the divisions that come the unification**; the power that divides is the power that unites.

blocks.title: Division of labor: the army
blocks.text: *Tikkun* is basically division of labor. It makes an army: each one *davka* in his own job, so that together they are a greater thing than if each guy did everything; then nobody would be a great driller.

blocks.title: A cluster of computers
blocks.text: A listener adds the computer cluster: a thousand computers dividing the work among their processors beat one supercomputer that does one thing at a time. *Davka* the division gives the inclusion.
So the army: a whole of inclusion, given by division, *davka* in the outside of the vessels: this guy army, that one navy, a gunner, a flyer. That makes the *Tikkun* of the army.

blocks.title: The cook and the dishwasher
blocks.text: It may seem to come from the inner intention joining them; not so much. *Tikkun* is a society where each has his own job, even a restaurant: that guy cooks, that guy washes dishes. If everybody does everything, it doesn't work so good, and there is no inclusion.
Not only that: too many cooks spoil the broth, like what happened with the Alter Rebbe, where everybody put salt in.

blocks.question: Why is the vessel batel to the light? It seems to come from the inner side of the vessels.
blocks.text: It seems so: an army works together not by outer functions but for a common goal, the inner side of the vessel: inside they're all Americans, which is why they joined, with one light, one *ratzon* (will). So it looks like the inner light.

Still, the *Tikkun* of the army comes *davka* from their division into functions, each doing his own and not the other's: that is how you fly a B-52. The same *ratzon* is very nice, but without a fine division it would be total *Tohu*.

blocks.title: The Indians and the white man's army
blocks.text: That is why the white man conquered the Indian. From the side of the light, their inner side, the Indians were more unified and more heroic. But each one was a whole brave, each one an army. You couldn't tell him: you can't have the glory, you'll be the guy who cleans the fish. "What do you mean? I'm a brave. I want to earn my feathers." In the white man's army some soldiers couldn't care less; they were career soldiers, not so brave. But they were separated into different functions. The Indians each wanted all the glory and would go whooping into battle.

sensitivity.reason: Pictures Native Americans as glory-seeking braves who "go whooping into battle".
sensitivity.publishable: That is why the white man conquered the Indian. From the side of the light, their inner side, the Indians were more unified and more heroic. But each one was a whole brave, each one an army. You couldn't tell him: you can't have the glory, you'll be the guy who cleans the fish. "What do you mean? I'm a brave. I want to earn my feathers." In the white man's army some soldiers couldn't care less; they were career soldiers, not so brave. But they were separated into different functions. The Indians each wanted all the glory.

phrases.he: שבזה דוקא יהיה ריבוי ההתכללות,
דבר והיפוכו כאחד
phrases.en: A thing and its opposite like one.

blocks.text: So division of labor makes the *Tikkun*, joining them into a higher grouping, like the white army. The Indians had none, though inside they were more unified, on principle, defending their own land (so too the Romans); specialists conquer a bunch of guys each a whole army by himself.

By the Indians there could be no inclusion: with no division, each did the same whole thing by himself, so inclusion of what? **A thing and its opposite like one**: one man does the hero's thing while another, a milquetoast pencil pusher writing reports in the office, seems the very opposite of a soldier. Try to get an Indian to push a pencil: "I want the glory. I'm a warrior."

sensitivity.reason: Continues the picture of the Indian as a glory-seeking warrior who would scorn a desk job.
sensitivity.publishable: By the Indians there could be no inclusion: with no division, each did the same whole thing by himself, so inclusion of what? **A thing and its opposite like one**: one man does the hero's thing while another, a milquetoast pencil pusher writing reports in the office, seems the very opposite of a soldier. Try to get a born warrior to push a pencil: he wants the glory.

sections.title: Adam of Tikkun: "behind and before You formed me"
sections.summary: The main thing of *Adam* of *Tikkun* is the division of organs. The matter comes both before the light, as its root and the vision of the end, and after it, in the physical body: the whole matter of the chain of descent, *yesh* from *yesh*.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר בחינת אדם דתיקון כו',
phrases.en: The main thing of *Adam* is that there's a division of organs.

phrases.he: שעליו אמר אחור וקדם צרתני, יצירה בגוף חומר דוקא כו' קדם, בבחינת החומר הפשוט שקדם לצורה, שהוא האור והוא בשרש הכלי שקדם לאור
ואחור, בכלי החומר שאחר האור והצורה כו'
phrases.en: That comes after the light, and it's through the actual physical thing.

phrases.he: ודי למבין וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר ביאור ענין זה באריכות (ודי למבין):

blocks.text: **The main thing of *Adam* is that there's a division of organs**: "behind and before You formed me". "Before": the body's final matter, the vision of how the whole army will move together, is in the root of the vessels, before the light.

"And behind": the matter also comes after the light, through the actual physical thing. This is the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) *yesh m'yesh* (something from something): the true *yesh*, the final person, comes from what preceded the light altogether.

reviewQuestions.question: How does the light of chesed shining in a vessel of gevura prove that inclusion comes from the vessels and not from the lights?
Why can one organ be cured by treating another, while failing sight from old age is not cured by strengthening the middos of the heart?
Why is it easier to act against your heart than to think against it, and what do Yael and the car salesman show?
In what way is even a death sentence, Haman's for example, not pure din once it comes to the deed?
If the vessel yields to its opposite light because of the inner intention, why can one angel still do only one mission?
How does the division of labor in an army make it more united than warriors who share one will?
